clue.text: Card game requiring players to hold an ace

indicators.note: the players are said to hold the next word, so it goes inside them

parts.note: the players in a play are its cast
A is the usual abbreviation for an ace in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A card game that needs its players to keep an ace back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' asks for the word an to go inside the players, not around them; 'ace' supplies the closing letter in the usual card-playing abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-type game played with two packs, so it is an example of a card game.

clue.text: Dog's nap is disturbed, having crowing bird around

definitions.note: the dog is, with 's as a link

indicators.note: having the bird around means it surrounds the jumbled letters

parts.note: a cockerel is a young cock that crows

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of nap is are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog's sleep is interrupted by a crowing rooster nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog's' is the definition plus a link 's (is); 'disturbed' scrambles nap is, and 'having ... around' wraps the young rooster round that scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a breed of small gun dog, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: News about Bosnia regularly ignored — go figure

indicators.note: about means the news letters go around the rest

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new, so news, as plural, gives two Ns

indicators.note: regularly ignored drops every other letter of Bosnia

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Reports about Bosnia are routinely neglected, which the speaker finds baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go figure' is an idiom of bafflement, but 'go' is wordplay; 'regularly ignored' leaves ONA from Bosnia.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a plane shape with nine sides, so it is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Spanish gentleman's second to last to sleep soundly?

indicators.note: second to last means the second letter is moved to the end

parts.note: señor is the Spanish for a gentleman; 's links to the instruction

explanation.surface: A Spaniard sleeps deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second to last' looks like 'penultimate' but means move the second letter to the end. 'Soundly' is the joke: a noisy sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing noisily while asleep is sleeping with sound, the question mark flagging the pun.

clue.text: A woman swallows a lot of salt water

indicators.note: swallows means the woman takes the next piece inside her

parts.note: a dame is a woman

indicators.note: a lot of means most of salt, leaving off its last letter

explanation.surface: A woman gulps down a mouthful of seawater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt water' suggests the sea, but it is two parts of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old jocular name for plain drinking water, the first man's drink.

clue.text: Plant first of nemesias towards the back

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like garden plant

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of nemesias

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: put a plant ahead of the nemesias, toward the back of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, astern is the nautical word for at or towards the rear.

clue.text: A guy skirting river gets lost

indicators.note: skirting means the guy runs around the river letter

parts.note: a stay is a guy rope bracing a mast

explanation.surface: Someone loses their way walking along a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' is not a man but a supporting rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off course is to wander, which is what 'gets lost' means as a phrase.

clue.text: Clement and Paddy scoffed

parts.note: a paddy is a fit of rage, a temper
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: Two men, Clement and Paddy, gobbled their food.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement and Paddy look like names; one is the definition (mild) and one a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is mild, a synonym.

clue.text: Right, Leo McKern's heading up cast as barrister

indicators.note: cast as in thrown, so these letters are shaken into a new order
heading picks the first letter of McKern's

explanation.surface: The actor Leo McKern was cast as a barrister, and his career took off.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo McKern did play this fictional barrister on TV, which makes 'cast' read as theatrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace Rumpole, of Rumpole of the Bailey, is a fictional Old Bailey barrister.

clue.text: Granny involves lad in backing Toc H perhaps

indicators.note: in places the granny-and-lad group inside the reversed letters that follow
backing means the word Toc is read from right to left
involves means the granny wraps around the lad

parts.note: nan is a familiar word for a grandmother
a lad is a son

explanation.surface: An old lady takes a boy along to help at the Toc H charity.
explanation.walkthrough: Toc H is a Christian charity, but the words split: Toc is wordplay, read backwards ('backing'), and H alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter H is not a vowel, so it is one example of the non-vowel class of letters.

clue.text: Do chapter on tragic heroine

indicators.note: in this across clue, on means the chapter comes after the heroine

parts.note: Mimi is the consumptive heroine who dies in Puccini's La Bohème

explanation.surface: Instructions to write a chapter about a doomed heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is not the verb of performing a task but of doing an impression of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To 'do' a celebrity is to impersonate them, which is a synonym for copying their mannerisms.

clue.text: Copper on case of theft was informed arrests have to make the grade

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: case of means only the outer letters of theft
arrests means the informed word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: heard means was informed
must means have to

explanation.surface: A police officer told about a theft makes arrests and is up to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means to reach the required standard, to succeed.

clue.text: Dog, not black, for harpy?

indicators.note: not says the black letter is to be left out of the dog

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Would a dog that is not black do in place of a harpy?
explanation.walkthrough: 'harpy' suggests the shrewish woman or Greek monster, but here it is the harpy eagle of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The harpy is one specific large tropical bird of prey, so it is an example of this raptor family.

clue.text: Pot caused Dicky to become this?

definitions.text: Pot caused Dicky to become this?

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Cannabis left someone called Dicky in a dazed state.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name but is the signal; the whole clue also describes the effect of smoking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dazed and vague after smoking cannabis is said, in slang, to be in this state.

clue.text: No-nonsense northern relation lost in York perhaps

indicators.note: in places the three short pieces inside the cathedral seat

parts.note: York is the seat of an archbishop, a see
a sib is a sibling, a brother or sister
L is the abbreviation for lost in sports results tables

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth northerner's family member goes missing in York.
explanation.walkthrough: York here is not the city but its diocese: a see is a bishop's area.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-nonsense person is practical and level-headed, a close synonym.

clue.text: Lying is popular with criminal

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
cum is Latin for with
bent is slang for corrupt, criminal

explanation.surface: A criminal who lies is popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' means resting on something, not telling untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: The technical sense of the adjective is resting or pressing on something, as one layer on another.

clue.text: God, say Hindus, originally possessing an elephant's head

definitions.text: God, say Hindus, originally possessing an elephant's head

indicators.note: possessing means the opening letters hold the following group inside them
originally asks for the first letter of each of God, say and Hindus
head picks the front letter of elephant's

explanation.surface: Describes a Hindu god who has the head of an elephant.
explanation.walkthrough: GSH holds AN plus E, giving G-ANE-SH; the whole clue also describes the deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The elephant-headed Hindu deity, remover of obstacles, is known by this name or as Ganesha.

clue.text: Boats travel by land so awkwardly

parts.note: go means travel

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters of land so are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: Boats are travelling over dry land, which is awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the flat-bottomed Venetian boats, so they are examples of boats.

clue.text: Make a show of influence

definitions.meaning: to pretend to have a feeling or manner, as in putting on an accent
to act upon or change something

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses of the verb: to feign something, and to have an effect on something.

clue.text: Orchestra stops to smoke? That's excessive!

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so the orchestra goes inside the smoke

parts.note: fume means smoke
LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: Orchestra members break off for a cigarette, too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulsome praise is overdone and effusive, so the adjective means overdone.

clue.text: Very forced smile concealing Charlie's gaffe

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: concealing means the rearranged smile hides the next letter inside it
forced suggests something twisted out of shape, so the letters of smile are rearranged

parts.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet; the 's links it to the definition

explanation.surface: An awkward grin masks someone called Charlie's embarrassing slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' turns SMILE into LEISM, and 'concealing' sets C inside it to make LECISM.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical blunder or a breach of etiquette is a faux pas, the core meaning of both words.

clue.text: Bill's singing well

definitions.meaning: a bill sent for payment; 's is a link
a singer with a good voice that day is said to be ...

explanation.surface: Bill has a fine voice.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name but is a demand for payment.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a commercial account requesting payment, a synonym for a bill.

clue.text: Authorise drug arrest by the French

parts.note: E is ecstasy, the drug
to nab is to arrest
le is French for the

explanation.surface: The French police are given permission to arrest a drug dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise is to give the means or power to do something.

clue.text: Captain invading valley, I reflected, is doomed

indicators.note: reflected, as in a mirror, means the whole assembly is read backwards
invading means the captain enters the valley

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley
Captain Nemo is the submarine commander in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: A captain marches into a valley and someone muses that it is doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invading' gives DENEMOLL; adding I and reading it all backwards ('reflected') gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ill-fated carries a bad portent, so it seems destined to fail.

clue.text: Rash man's keeping WWII bomb around

indicators.note: keeping means the man's letters hold the bomb inside

parts.note: man's, as in a man is, gives he's

indicators.note: around turns the bomb's letters back to front

parts.note: the V1 was the German flying bomb of the Second World War, written here VI

explanation.surface: A reckless man holds on to an old wartime bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like an adjective for the man but is the noun: a skin eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Hives, or urticaria, is an itchy skin eruption, a type of rash.

clue.text: One may laugh, showing some healthy enamel

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grinning person shows off their healthy teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted species is famous for a cackling call like human laughter.

clue.text: Cut Hank on vacation some slack

indicators.note: cut means the hank loses its final letter

parts.note: a hank is a coiled loop of wool or rope

indicators.note: on vacation means some is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Give someone called Hank a little leeway while away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'cut someone some slack' is broken up: Hank is a coil of yarn, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A slack rope is not taut, a close synonym.

clue.text: All-in wrestling with bare stage performer

indicators.note: wrestling suggests the letters grappling and tumbling into a new order

explanation.surface: No-holds-barred wrestling done with bare skin.
explanation.walkthrough: All-in wrestling is a real freestyle sport, which hides the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet dancer performs on stage, so she is one kind of stage performer.

clue.text: Crossword solver, as it were, gets a seat

definitions.meaning: a coined word: the person a crossword compiler sets puzzles for
a sofa for two or more people

explanation.surface: A puzzle fan sits down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it were' signals a made-up word: the compiler is the setter, so the solver is the one set for.
explanation.definitionFit: The playful coinage is matched by a real word for a long upholstered sofa.

clue.text: Dread getting into offspring's tangle?

indicators.note: getting into puts dread inside the offspring

parts.note: seed means offspring, as in biblical descendants; the 's means is
awe is reverential fear, dread

explanation.surface: Fear causing a mess among one's children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangle' is not a muddle but a type of large brown kelp; the question mark marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangle is a name for oarweed, a kind of kelp, so it is one example of marine algae.
